title: Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity?
content_md: I was recently asked to speak at an event but was unable to accept due to a prior speaking commitment on the same day. This, in and of itself, is not unusual – it happens fairly often. What happened about a week later, however, gave me some interesting food for thought. Someone that was available and had agreed to speak at the event in my place approached me to ask for content for the talk. Now, I am always happy to help someone work through what type of content might be interesting and appealing to the audience, as well as to point them in the right direction regarding developing that content. The manner in which this person approached me was not that, unfortunately. In the moment, I tried to guide the individual in a helpful way. Only later, after analyzing the interaction a bit more, did I realize something. Essentially, the person approached me as people approach AI. How so? Rather than ask for guidance, tips, lessons learned from experience, dos and don’ts, etc., the person basically sent me a prompt. Something that when I thought about it later sounded a lot like “Tell me the most interesting points on topic X and provide me a presentation on that topic.” This experience got me thinking. Are there ways in which AI could actually be harming us as a security industry? Of course, I know that there are many use cases for which AI helps increase productivity, efficiency, and has other benefits.
